meta_description: Trial patient-matching grounded in protocol criteria — screen-fail rate down 28% and enrollment timelines met on three of three studies

blocks.x: Trial patient-matching grounded in protocol criteria, screen-fail rate down 28% and enrollment timelines met on three of three studies

Identity withheld, a global CRO whose enrollment engine was coordinator memory: the right patients existed in referring networks, but nobody could search them against a protocol's fine print. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline across three studies: 41% screen-fail rate on first-line candidates, coordinators hand-screening 60 records per enrolled patient, and two studies forecasting missed enrollment milestones.
Protocol criteria lived in PDFs; candidate records lived in EHRs. Every match was a human crosswalk between two languages, done under enrollment pressure.

We built matching on retrieval: protocol eligibility criteria parsed into a machine-checkable form with the coordinator reviewing each interpretation, candidate records normalized across referring EHRs, and match rankings produced with every criterion hit cited to its source. Coordinators approve with evidence attached; the study dashboard shows exactly which criterion loses candidates.
